newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON-HOLYFIELD II MORE OF A MENTAL THING.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON-HOLYFIELD II MORE OF A MENTAL THING.

text.p: Evander Holyfield and Mike Tyson both expect their World Boxing Association heavyweight title bout Saturday to be as much of a "mental" war as their last fight was a bruising physical battle.

"This fight is much more mental than anybody would have ever imagined," Holyfield said at a joint news conference at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas Wednesday. "When both are in (top) physical condition, then the mental takes over in this game."

Holyfield won the title last November in the 11th round by taking the fight to the hard-hitting Tyson, opening up a cut over his eye in the sixth round and later catching him with a short left to the head that put him on the canvas -- only the second time "Iron Mike" had ever been knocked down.

Holyfield effectively negated the then-champion's one-dimensional style by counter-punching to the body and blocking Tyson's lethal left hook. The referee stopped the fight when Holyfield pummeled Tyson with nine unanswered punches.
After that physical battle, both camps are pointing to brain power as a key to Saturday's fight, dubbed "The Sound and the Fury.
Tyson, a man of few words, let his co-manager do the talking when asked about the mind games that could influence the outcome.
"This fight is mental," John Horne told reporters.
"We didn't see anything in the first fight that Mike Tyson can't handle," he added, playing a little mind game of his own.
"I believe Mike Tyson will be the winner by a knockout this time," said Horne in the only concrete prediction by either of the two camps, who have stayed publicly respectful of each other.

Holyfield was an overwhelming 25-1 underdog a week before the November 9 bout and was still a 4-1 outsider by the time he climbed in the ring. But he attributed his win to mental staying power born of his devout Christianity. Tyson for his part is a convert to Islam.

Tyson, the youngest man to be world heavyweight champion at the age of 20 when he beat Trevor Berbick in 1986, was embarrassed in November when the referee stepped in to save him from further punishment.
Asked Wednesday if he felt he had made any mistakes last time and how he would correct them, Tyson grinned broadly and said: "Sure, I lost the fight. We'll correct it by winning."
Tyson has been installed as a 2-1 favourite by Las Vegas oddsmakers.
"I am in better shape than last time and I look forward to beating him this time," said Tyson, whose record is 45 wins and only two losses.
But Holyfield (33-3) was sure he would repeat the victory that made him only the second three-time world champion, after Muhammad Ali.
"I am sure Team Tyson has explored the (video) tape and found a way to beat the guy who fought on November 9. But I am a different guy," he said.

Asked if it was a spiritual battle, the 6-foot-2-1/2-inch (1.89 metres) Holyfield warmed to the subject. "My body does what my mind tells it to do. I have been fighting 26 years and prayer has always kept me focused," he said.
Meanwhile, the 5-foot-11-1/2-inch (1.82 metres) Tyson refused to be drawn on what tactics he would employ against a man he said he has great respect for.
"I am confident I am going to win, and he will not have the championship come Saturday night."
The fight was originally scheduled for May, but was postponed when Tyson cut his eye in March. What effect would the delay have?
"We are both in great shape, but maybe with more time to train, that will be advantageous,"said Tyson.
Holyfield was succinct. "I am peaking at the right time," he said.

Promoter Don King said the quality of the two heavyweights guaranteed that the estimated three billion worldwide TV audience would see a fight even better than Ali's "Thrilla in Manila" with Joe Frazier or "Rumble in the Jungle" with George Foreman.

On the undercard Saturday, Mexico's Julio Cesar Chavez will be bidding for his 100th career win when he fights Larry Daniel La Coursiere in a super lightweight bout, and Christy Martin and Andrea DeShong will fight for a WBC women's lightweight title.
